clue.text: Ring the Rear Admiral it's a fantastic idea

parts.note: to ring a bell is to chime

explanation.surface: A naval officer's grand scheme strikes everyone as fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild, impossible fancy, named after the monstrous beast of Greek myth.

clue.text: Sudden change in EC policy on grain

parts.note: CAP is the Common Agricultural Policy of the European Community
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: European farm policy on cereal crops abruptly shifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim or an impulsive change of mind.

clue.text: One eminent cast in disarray long, long ago

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: disarray shows the letters of eminent cast in are jumbled

explanation.surface: A distinguished person was thrown into chaos ages back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but belongs to the anagram material, with 'disarray' alone as the signal; 'cast' also tempts as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the distant past, in olden days.

clue.text: City house may resound

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A town dwelling might ring with noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to reverberate, as a sound repeated off walls.

clue.text: Risked getting burnt as a martyr

explanation.surface: A martyr took a chance and was burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in jeopardy, and literally describes someone tied to a post to be burnt.

clue.text: Speed at which sailor turns east

indicators.note: turns tells us the sailor's word is read from right to left

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A sailor heading eastward sets the pace of a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rate is a measure of how fast something goes, a synonym of velocity.

clue.text: Dash across the road and get knocked down

explanation.surface: Sprint over the street and get hit by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to hurry across briefly, and also to be struck by a vehicle.

clue.text: Change course to get equestrian equipment

explanation.surface: A rider changes direction to fetch horse gear.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing it means to turn into the wind, and it is also the saddlery used for riding horses.

clue.text: Enticed fill-in typist to make hay

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
to ted is to spread grass out to dry as hay

explanation.surface: A temporary secretary was lured into a farming job.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempted means lured or persuaded by temptation.

clue.text: A pressman sure to die after being replaced

indicators.note: being replaced shows the letters of sure to die after are put in new places

explanation.surface: A journalist is certain to perish once supplanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper journalist who edits the paper's longer articles is a kind of pressman.

clue.text: A sweet and lovely English complexion

explanation.surface: A dessert and the fair skin of an English rose.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish is fruit served with dairy topping, and the phrase also describes a fair, rosy complexion.

clue.text: Popular church measure

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A well-loved church's yardstick.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is an imperial unit of length, a small measure of about two and a half centimetres.

clue.text: The greeting to soothe wounded feelings?

explanation.surface: A kind hello meant to calm someone who has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is Latin: 'salve' is a Roman word of welcome, pronounced in two syllables.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin greeting means hail, and as an English verb it means to ease or comfort, as an ointment does.

clue.text: A little bird working hard

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird busily occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone busily engaged in an activity, toiling away.

clue.text: Essential for Miss Singleton to include it

indicators.note: to include tells us the presenter's name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Valerie Singleton was a Blue Peter presenter on BBC children's television

explanation.surface: A requirement for a well-known presenter to feature something.
explanation.walkthrough: Valerie (Val) Singleton was a long-serving presenter of Blue Peter, a British children's TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Escape from a feeling of loneliness

parts.note: a void is an empty, lonely feeling

explanation.surface: Fleeing an empty, lonely sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to keep away from or evade it.

clue.text: Solitary child follows before

indicators.note: follows tells us the child's word comes after the word for before

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A lonely child trails behind someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a religious recluse who lives alone.

clue.text: Embarrassed about constantly being regarded with awe

indicators.note: about tells us the word for embarrassed goes around the other piece

parts.note: embarrassed people go red in the face
ever means always or constantly

explanation.surface: Someone constantly blushing while being admired.
explanation.definitionFit: To be revered is to be deeply respected and venerated.

clue.text: Where models tread with feline grace?

definitions.text: Where models tread with feline grace?

parts.words: Where models tread with feline grace?
parts.note: the fashion runway, read literally as a stroll for a cat

explanation.surface: Fashion models move with the poise of cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A catwalk is the narrow raised runway on which models parade clothes at a fashion show.

clue.text: Strangely enough, it's a breakdown!

parts.note: the word for bursting into laughter also names a mental collapse

explanation.surface: An odd remark that something has collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack-up is a nervous collapse, though to crack up is also to laugh helplessly.

clue.text: Dishonest conduct by rising cleric in American recession

indicators.note: in tells us the turned cleric goes inside the turned American
recession, a moving backwards, tells us the American is read in reverse

parts.note: a Yank is an American

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend, a cleric

explanation.surface: Fraud by a clergyman climbing the ranks during an economic slump in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavery is roguish trickery, the behaviour of a knave or scoundrel.

clue.text: China seems in turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil shows the letters of seems in are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: China appears to be in political upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but it is porcelain; 'in' is part of the fodder, with 'turmoil' alone as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen is a fine German porcelain, the first true hard-paste ware made in Europe.

clue.text: A joke delivered in my autocratic style

indicators.note: delivered in tells us the joke is placed inside the word my

parts.note: taken as written
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A gag told in my high-handed manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is the form of address for a sovereign, a ruler with supreme power.

clue.text: Refusal by colliery to take on English candidate

parts.note: no is a refusal
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A coal pit turns down hiring an English applicant.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person put forward for a post or award.

clue.text: Keen for commercial to be shown around six

indicators.note: shown around tells us the commercial's letters wrap the number

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Eager for an advert to run at six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or enthusiastic.

clue.text: Instrument used to keep out a little woman

parts.note: to ban is to exclude or keep out
Jo March is one of the sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A tool used to bar a small woman from entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little woman' points to Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women, whose heroine is Jo.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed musical instrument with a round drum-like body.

clue.text: A water barrier built by man

parts.note: a dam holds back water

explanation.surface: A barrier to water constructed by human hands.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam is the first man, and his name is Hebrew for human being.

clue.text: Pureed fruit and trifle

explanation.surface: Two kinds of fruit-based pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is a dessert of pureed fruit and cream; to fool about is to trifle. 'trifle' is also a dessert, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The dessert is crushed fruit folded into cream, and to fool with something is to toy with it.

clue.text: Watch TV to form an opinion

explanation.surface: Seeing television in order to make up one's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Television audiences are viewers, and a personal opinion is a point of view.

clue.text: Remove only trousers to stay cool

definitions.text: Remove only trousers to stay cool

parts.words: Remove only trousers to stay cool
parts.note: taking off just the lower garment leaves the top one on; the phrase also means remain calm

explanation.surface: Advice on undressing partly in hot weather.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stay calm and not lose one's temper.

clue.text: Fellow reclined to strip off

parts.note: lay is the past tense of lie, to recline

explanation.surface: A man lay down so he could undress.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay is to peel the skin off, so it means to strip away.

clue.text: Yet we're resolved to get a conifer

indicators.note: resolved, read as re-solved, tells us the letters of yet we're are worked out afresh

explanation.surface: Even so, we are determined to obtain an evergreen.
explanation.definitionFit: The yew is an evergreen tree bearing needles, a member of the conifer group.
